DEVELOPER INSIGHTS

From Company Profile to Project Evidence: How to Assess a Specialist

Use credentials as the start of due diligence, then ask for relevant detail.

In this insight

Read the profile with the project in mindPreserve the attribution of experienceAsk for evidence that resolves a questionTranslate confidence into contract clarityFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Read the profile with the project in mind

A company profile introduces services, people, equipment and selected experience. Its value is strongest when the buyer connects those claims to the current project. Identify which capabilities are relevant and which require further discussion. A broad experience statement should not replace questions about the proposed team, method, availability and responsibility for this particular scope.

Preserve the attribution of experience

Projects may belong to the company, a predecessor business, a joint venture or a strategic partner. Keep those distinctions visible when assessing capability. Ask what role was performed and what evidence can be shared. This gives a more accurate view of the experience available to the proposed team without assuming that every project shown represents the same contractual role.

Ask for evidence that resolves a question

Request relevant project details, references or examples of deliverables where appropriate and permitted. Explain what you are trying to assess, such as coordination experience, documentation quality or a similar site constraint. Focused questions are more productive than asking for an ever-larger portfolio. Respect confidentiality while seeking enough detail to support an informed appointment.

Translate confidence into contract clarity

Once a specialist is selected, ensure the agreed team, scope, interfaces and deliverables are reflected in the appointment. A positive impression from the profile should lead to a clear delivery basis, not substitute for one. The strongest commercial relationship combines credible experience with precise commitments, transparent assumptions and a practical process for handling the uncertainties that remain.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Assess credentials against the actual project.
  • Keep company, predecessor and partner experience distinct.
  • Convert agreed capability into explicit delivery commitments.

References & further reading

  • Further reading: FHWA — Geotechnical technical guidance

International references provide technical context; applicable local requirements and the project engineer’s decisions govern the actual works.
